summary: In a culture filled with competing messages, how can we faithfully teach children the truth while also modeling love and compassion toward those who have rejected it?

title: How to Fire Someone at a Christian Organization
summary: If managers do their jobs well, believe that God is sovereign, and bring the love of Christ even into hard conversations, everyone will be better off.
summary_zh: 如果管理者能做好自己的工作，相信神掌管一切，即使在艰难的谈话中也能流露出基督的爱，那么每个人都会受益。
title_zh: 如何在基督教组织中解雇某人
content: Over the course of my career, I’ve participated in more than 190 exits of employees, whether I was coaching a manager, planning upstream, sitting in on calls, or orchestrating layoffs. Each time was tough. Parting ways with an employee is one of the heaviest things a manager does. Doing it both clearly and kindly takes a lot of preparation and emotional regulation. In a faith-based workplace, these decisions can be even more surprising and hurtful, because managers try to spare the discomfort of a conversation about performance under any number of banners of being “kind.” How should we think about this as Christians who manage other Christians? Why Good Work Is Important A church’s mission is to spread the good news of Jesus, create ways for people to know him more deeply, and love our neighbors. A Christian nonprofit’s purpose is adjacent—to provide mercy, justice, evangelism, or discipleship while pointing people to Christ and their local church. This work happens through ministry and outreach staff, but also through effective operations. Doing this work takes all types of roles: pastors, administrators, and ministry coordinators; managers, accountants, and musicians; executive admins, facilities operators, and IT teams. Much of what it takes to run a church or Christian organization happens outside the hours of direct ministry. To do any of this well, churches and nonprofits must hire capable people who can effectively perform their duties and steward the mission. When managers in a secular workplace don’t hire wisely, I’ve seen the result in poor functional performance, departmental infighting, disengagement, acrimonious exits, and abuse of company resources. In a faith-based organization or church, you may get a mix of this and something worse: the spread of the gospel can be compromised too. Upstream Work for Managers As a manager, if you notice someone isn’t performing well, the best time to start talking about it isn’t at the exit conversation. It’s way upstream from that. Your core job is to ensure your people have what they need to be successful. That includes clear expectations, communication of what success looks like, feedback on performance, and accountability for meeting those standards. Ideally, you’re doing these on a regular basis in one-on-one meetings  and in performance check-ins throughout the year. Churches and nonprofits must hire capable people who can effectively perform their duties and steward the mission. This is a manager’s job, and faith-based organizations don’t have a softer standard. Where I’ve seen termination decisions and conversations go south—in Christian organizations or elsewhere—is when a manager doesn’t understand this. (Or, worse, they understand it but think that somehow it doesn’t apply to them.) Speaking to an employee about parting ways because you’ve consistently documented underperformance is a rough conversation. It’s far worse when your failure to give regular feedback leaves an employee blindsided, confused, and hurt when you need to broach termination. Often, that failure is rooted in a desire to avoid conflict or hurt feelings. The manager would rather spare himself the discomfort of a direct conversation. In a Christian organization, this impulse pulls hard. The employees under your care all love Jesus. They’re there to promote the church’s mission and spread the gospel. You may even sit shoulder to shoulder in the pews with them on Sundays. But James 4:17 has a word for managers who fail to do the difficult work: “Whoever knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, for him it is sin.” Colossians 4:1 underlines this: “Masters, treat your bondservants justly and fairly, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.” I’ve watched managers avoid the perceived sin of commission (telling someone he’s doing a poor job in his role) and step right into the sin of omission (letting the problem fester until the employee is struggling and a termination conversation seems inevit

title: Why Christianity Explains Our Deepest Longings
summary: ‘Why Christianity Makes Sense’ offers a compelling argument that Christianity explains the condition of both the world and the human heart.
summary_zh: 《基督教为何有道理》提出一个令人信服的论点，即基督教解释了世界和人心两种状态。
title_zh: 为什么基督教能够解释我们最深切的渴望
content: Throughout church history, God has raised up faithful voices to speak the gospel to each generation. The apostle Paul traveled through much of the known world, preaching in synagogues and public settings. In Athens, he used the questions the culture was asking as a platform from which to proclaim the gospel. Similarly, Augustine, Anselm, Blaise Pascal, C. S. Lewis, Tim Keller, and many others helped readers see Christianity’s coherence amid the questions and assumptions of their times. Through his online ministry, Truth Unites , Gavin Ortlund fills that sort of role in our cultural moment. In Why Christianity Makes Sense: A Book About Jesus, the Mysteries of the World, and the Longings in Your Heart , Ortlund offers an accessible defense of the faith for readers unsure whether Christianity can withstand serious examination. It’s also a useful tool for discipling believers bombarded with hard questions about Christianity on the internet. Ortlund’s goal is to show “why it makes sense to be a Christian” (xiii). Ortlund’s particular strength is that he recognizes our questions aren’t merely intellectual. They arise from deeper longings for meaning, purpose, and transcendence. Unknown God In Athens, Paul thoughtfully noticed an altar established “to the unknown god” (Acts 17:23). He didn’t mock them for it. Every generation builds an altar of its own. Augustine called it the restless heart; Lewis called it Sehnsucht , the longing that joy itself cannot satisfy. Keller called the traces it leaves behind clues . Ortlund has a name for it: “the ache.” Ortlund doesn’t begin with a technical exposition of the ache but by showing it’s the desire behind every altar to every unknown god. He asks, “Are you genuinely curious about what life means—why you’re here, and what it’s all for?” (xi). The ache is the restless longing for the transcendent that we can’t put into words. Just as hunger implies we live in a world where food is meant to fuel our bodies, so the desire for meaning points to the existence of something that will satisfy that desire. So many counterfeits promise to satisfy our desire for God. Many people have learned to deny any sense of longing for the divine or simply scroll past the question before it finishes loading in their minds. Just as hunger implies we live in a world where food is meant to fuel our bodies, so the desire for meaning points to the existence of something that will satisfy that desire. In a culture where the most shocking content on social media becomes boring, it’s worth drawing attention to Jesus’s radical claims. “He claimed to be the way, the truth, and the life,” notes Ortlund. “Muhammad taught the five pillars, Buddha spoke of enlightenment, Confucius pointed to the Way, but Jesus pointed to himself as the answer. In fact, Jesus claimed to be God” (104). The claim is preposterous, unless it’s true. So Ortlund asks his readers to put on their thinking caps: “What if God is real, and Jesus is this God, showing up in history to reveal himself to us? Why not? Is it really all that much crazier than the alternatives?” (104). It’s not. And more importantly, the solution Jesus offers is the most complete answer to the ache. This message deserves to be proclaimed in public. In the Marketplace When Paul was in Athens, he “reasoned . . . in the marketplace” (Acts 17:17), the agora, which is where ideas were exchanged. Our modern agora is increasingly virtual, less of a town square and more like the comment section of a microvlog. Ortlund has excelled in this space, making hard things plain in his videos without making them small. His talent for public communication comes through in this book. For example, Ortlund tackles divine hiddenness: Have you ever wondered why, if God is indeed real, his existence isn’t completely obvious? Why are religious matters so ambiguous ? Wouldn’t a loving God want to make things clear to us? (176) It’s an intuitive argument that undermines the sense that the ache is a longing

这么多假货承诺满足我们对上帝的渴望. 许多人已经学会否认任何对神的渴望感,或者在问题进入他们的脑海之前,简单地将问题卷过。 正如饥饿意味着我们生活在一个粮食本意在促进我们身体的世界中一样,因此,对含义的渴望表明存在满足这种愿望的东西。

title: Small-Church Elders, Here’s How to Give Your Pastor a Sabbatical
summary: Our church has 74 members and two lay elders. Here’s how we raised up five men to preach seven expository sermons and give our pastor a summer sabbatical.
summary_zh: 我们的教会共有74名会友和两名平信徒长老。以下是我们如何培养五位弟兄来宣讲七篇解经性讲道，并让我们的牧师度过一个夏季安息假。
title_zh: 小型教会的长老们，以下是为你们的牧师安排安息假的方式
content: “He should have had a sabbatical six years ago,” my fellow elder said. “I know,” I said. “We know he needs it, but how are we going to do this? We have full-time jobs and young families.” “Well, the cattle on thousand hills are the Lord’s. Let’s ask him to provide it.” I nodded in agreement, but honestly, cattle felt like less of an ask for our church. Our church consists of 74 members. We have one full-time pastor and two lay elders. And yet, exactly two years after that initial elders’ meeting, we managed to give our pastor a much-needed, six-week summer sabbatical. Five male members of our church delivered seven expository and Christ-exalting sermons. God was glorified, our pastor rested, and our church loved it. We preached through an entire book of the Bible (Habakkuk). We preached a doctrinal sermon from our confession of faith (on baptism and Communion). Two men preached for the first time. The men ranged from age 20 to 46, and I was the seasoned preacher with 25 sermons under my belt. So how did we pull this off? 1. We prayed. We knew we couldn’t do this. Only God could. This reality framed our prayers over the next two years. God was glorified, our pastor rested, and our church loved it. We came to realize that just as the Sabbath was a gift from God to man (Mark 2:27), so a sabbatical is a gift from God to a pastor. As lay elders, we were called to take steps of faith to this end while relying on the Holy Spirit’s leading and enablement. Just as Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath (Matt. 12:8), so too is he Lord of a sabbatical. As we began to make plans, we prayed that we’d hold them with an open hand and continually lay them at the feet of Jesus. We borrowed words from Jehoshaphat (2 Chron. 20:12) for our prayer in this season: “Lord, we do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.” 2. We planned backward. We began by identifying the ideal time of year for the sabbatical. We landed on July and August, since that’s when church programming is minimal and vacations are in vogue among our congregation. This decision indirectly led us to the length of sabbatical we felt could responsibly plan for: six weeks. From there, we planned backward. The first Sunday we discussed was the Sunday our pastor would return. How did we want our brother and his wife to reintegrate into the church? We decided we wanted him to feel the warmth of our church’s love in his homecoming without being distracted by sermon preparation. So we chose to begin and end his sabbatical on Fridays. This meant our pastor had a workweek before leaving, so he could help with administrative functions. And by returning from the sabbatical on a Friday, he’d be able to join us for an elder meeting to get updates on members prior to attending church two days later. Preaching could wait another week. We created a two-year timeline that included all of the specific events and developments we thought could be feasible with the Lord’s help. This timeline helped us to answer several looming questions: Should we start the sabbatical by sending our pastor somewhere to create physical and emotional separation between him and our congregation? We agreed we should. We also felt this was an opportunity to invite our church to be generous and to tangibly show their love to our pastor of 12 years and his wife by paying for this trip. How many of our male members would be willing to assist with the preaching? We estimated three to four. How and when would we get them trained? This was the hardest question to answer but also the most rewarding part of this process. 3. We created a brotherhood. We realized our biggest hurdle would be recruiting and training men to aid in the preaching. To address the issue, we settled on offering a six-week preaching cohort during the summer prior to the sabbatical. To identify potential men for the cohort, we asked, “Which men currently do Scripture readings and prayers exceptionally well in our worship services?” Then we talked to each man indiv

content: When you really want to dive into the details of big questions about public policy—how we can live better together—you run into two problems: The experts and other stakeholders don’t want to consider Christian arguments, and Christians don’t want to engage in the details. That combination of a Christian argument from a legal expert was rare when Matt Martens’s book Reforming Criminal Justice: A Christian Proposal came out in 2023 from Crossway. And it’s still rare today. Matt is a trial lawyer and partner at an international law firm in Washington, DC. He and his wife are members at Capitol Hill Baptist Church, and they have two sons and a daughter. I read this book when it came out, and it’s stuck with me. Just the other day, I was thinking about the book when talking to one of my pastors, who was preparing to preach from 1 Peter on justice and obeying authorities. I thought about how I’d want to see the criminal justice system reformed if there were a good shot I’d be either a victim or criminal defendant. Isn’t that the law summed up in loving our neighbors as ourselves? From the death penalty to AI to the decline of violent crime—Matt and I covered a great deal. title: The Cumulative Effect of Thousands of Family Bible Times
summary: When your kids are inattentive or disruptive, don’t be overly discouraged. If the milk spills, if a fight erupts, all is not lost.
summary_zh: 当您的孩子注意力不集中或行为扰乱时，不要过于沮丧。如果牛奶洒了，如果发生了争吵，一切都还没完。
title_zh: 数千次家庭查经的累积效应
content: The alarm goes off, and another busy day begins. Getting kids up and ready for school, meal prep, work, after-school activities. Before you know it, the day is racing to its close. And you’re exhausted again. As Christian parents, we want our lives to count for Christ. We sincerely want our children to live their lives for Christ too. We want them to be changed by the same amazing grace that has transformed us. But how does this happen? How can we find the time and energy to effectively disciple our kids? Where will we find the creativity and passion to teach them what matters most? If you’re discouraged by your limited time and ability to shepherd your children, consider the cumulative effects of thousands of family Bible readings over the course of many years. Think Small What if a brief Bible reading today, a couple more later this week, and a few more next week eventually became a pattern, a deeply rooted habit for your family? Small investments of time and intentionality can make a big difference over a couple decades. Small investments of time and intentionality can make a big difference over the span of a couple decades. Years ago, Trevin Wax wrote an article titled “ 1000 Sermons Will Change Your Life .” What he says to pastors about preaching also applies to parents who lead their kids in family Bible reading: Pastors, don’t underestimate the cumulative effect of your preaching. You are not dumping information into brains. You are forming the habits of your people, teaching them how to read and understand and apply the Bible for themselves. Similarly in family life, our discipleship has cumulative effects that may not come to fruition for years. As parents, we’re in this for the long haul. If your children live in your home from birth to age 18, that’s 6,570 days. If you read the Bible together on average every third day, that’s 2,190 Bible readings over the course of your sons’ and daughters’ childhood and teenage years. Keep that big picture in mind when you feel defeated after a couple days on the go, when those family discipleship moments have eluded you. Think of Timothy, who was acquainted with the sacred writings from childhood because of his mother’s and grandmother’s faithful witness (2 Tim. 1:5; 3:14–15). May we be influential parents like them, who little by little and day by day pass on our life of faith to the next generation. Be Consistent, Establish a Habit With the long view in mind, think small in terms of your goals for this week, month, or year. Aim for consistency, for establishing a habit that you can pray will take root in your kids’ lives. Joe Carter recently shared the results of a sociological study of how faith moves across generations. He summarized the findings: The behaviors that most strongly predict lasting faith are active and verbal: praying together as a family, saying grace, embedding faith in the rhythm of the week rather than reserving it for Sunday, and, above all, talking about it. Children raised in homes where faith was discussed at least several times a week were more than twice as likely to attend church, pray daily, and rate religion as very important in young adulthood. The simplest way to put this truth into practice in your home is by creating a rhythm of opening the Bible regularly, reading some verses, and discussing them. You may never have a sense that one particular devotional was transformative. But keep at it. When your kids are inattentive or disruptive, don’t be overly discouraged. If the milk spills, if a fight erupts, all is not lost. Resist the temptation to quit. Come back to the reading the next day, or the day after that. Keep finding times to open the Bible with your family. Let the Word Do the Heavy Lifting Another deterrent that may get in the way of family discipleship is “the intimidation factor.” If you feel ill-equipped to teach the Bible to your kids, you may be inclined to leave that task to Sunday school teachers and youth pastors. summary_zh: 自2017年以来，沙赫扎德·马西一直在祈祷正义的到来。他因莫须有的罪名被捕时年仅16岁，自2022年以来一直在等待被处以绞刑。九年后，美国中心
title_zh: 为巴基斯坦基督徒的释放而进行的呼吁工作变得更加紧迫
content: Shahzad Masih has been praying for justice since 2017. He was just 16 years old when he was arrested on false charges, and has been waiting to be hanged since 2022. Nine years later, the American Center for Law and Justice (ACLJ), through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), is continuing to advocate for his release, Christian Daily International reported. In 2017, Masih was working as a janitor at a hospital when a Muslim coworker asked him about his belief in Jesus. As he explained his faith, he mentioned a comment made by a family friend that was spoken against the Prophet Muhammad, which offended the coworker and ended the conversation. The coworker belonged to Tehreek-e-Tahfuz-e-Islam, a conservative Islamic group in Pakistan. Members of the group heard about their conversation and confronted the Masih. Though he tried to clarify the situation, he was handed over to the police on July 13, 2017, and was questioned without legal representation before being imprisoned. In November 2022, according to Section 295C of the Pakistan Penal Code, he was sentenced to death for the “use of derogatory remarks, etc. in respect of the Holy Prophet.” Since then, he has been waiting to be hanged for his unjust sentence. The United Nations has called for his immediate release, stating that these decisions deny his right to “freedom of expression.” OLA has supported him and filed an appeal for his freedom four times, but the Lahore High Court has yet to hear his case. “Shahzad Masih was just 16 years old when he was arrested, and nine years later, he remains on death row for allegedly reporting someone else’s words,” said CeCe Heil, senior counsel and international legal director for the ACLJ. “We urge Pakistani authorities to uphold fundamental human rights, overturn this unjust conviction, and bring Shahzad Masih home to his family.” One of Many As more stories of Christians being imprisoned for false blasphemy accusations arise this year — including Amir Peter , who was tried before by a Lahore court in 2024 and died in custody in July — ACLJ is committed more than ever to fighting for the life of this young Christian. “This is the ultimate abominable human rights violation, and we’ll take this case all the way to Pakistan’s Supreme Court,” the advocacy group wrote . Open Doors ranks Pakistan as the eighth most dangerous place to be a Christian in the world. They are constantly subjected to persecution through discrimination, death threats, mob violence, imprisonment, and death, through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), continues. title: Vietnam Demolishes Historic Catholic Property Amid Church Land Dispute
summary: Vietnamese authorities demolished a historic building belonging to the Redemptorist Catholic community in the central city of Huế on Tuesday, escalating a decades-long dispute over church property and
summary_zh: 周二，越南当局拆除了位于中部城市顺化的一座属于救赎会天主教团体的历史建筑，加剧了长达数十年来围绕教会财产和
title_zh: 越南在教会土地纠纷中拆除历史悠久的天主教建筑
content: Vietnamese authorities demolished a historic building belonging to the Redemptorist Catholic community in the central city of Huế on Tuesday, escalating a decades-long dispute over church property and raising renewed concerns about religious freedom in the communist-governed country. The demolition of the L’Accueil building followed the deployment of police by local authorities to block roads surrounding the Redemptorist monastery and Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church. Electricity to the area was also cut, preventing some parishioners from reaching the church to attend Mass or express solidarity with the religious community. According to the Redemptorists, heavy machinery began demolishing the structure while priests, religious brothers, and parishioners gathered nearby in prayer. The demolition continued through Nov. 18, leaving the property leveled and fenced off. The Redemptorist Provincial Chapter of Vietnam condemned the operation, arguing that authorities proceeded despite unresolved legal questions and repeated requests to review the property’s ownership. “Justice cannot be established through force, and the truth cannot be erased along with the structures that have been demolished,” the congregation said in a Nov. 17 statement as the demolition was proceeding. Communist Land Takeover The dispute centers on land that the Redemptorists purchased in 1930. According to historical documentation cited by the religious order, Huế municipal authorities formally recognized the congregation’s ownership in 1971. The L’Accueil complex was subsequently developed on the property between 1938 and 1943. It served as a center for educational, cultural, and community activities, housing a library, auditorium, and reading room. A sawmill was also established on the grounds in the 1950s, providing local employment. Following the communist takeover of South Vietnam in 1975, the government’s relationship with religious institutions changed significantly. Church properties throughout the country came under increasing state control, with religious communities frequently losing access to land and buildings they had previously owned. The Redemptorists maintain that they never voluntarily surrendered their rights to the L’Accueil property. They acknowledge that the congregation transferred assets associated with a sawmill to the state in 1978, but argue that the transfer did not include the land itself. Authorities subsequently assigned the property to government-controlled institutions. The remaining parcel, measuring about 2,550 square meters, is currently managed by a local sports vocational school. Recent Efforts The congregation has sought the property’s return since 1994. Its most recent formal complaint, submitted to the Huế People’s Committee on Oct. 24, requested recognition of its land-use rights and clarification of the property’s legal status. Authorities reportedly rejected the complaint in a Nov. 8 response, stating that it had no basis for consideration. A notice posted at the property in October announced plans to develop a public park and parking lot on the site. Local authorities have defended the project as serving public interests, including improving traffic conditions and providing additional green space in a densely populated area. Vietnamese law establishes that land is collectively owned by the people and administered by the state. Government authorities have also invoked a 2003 National Assembly resolution that generally prevents reconsideration of certain land and housing arrangements established before July 1, 1991. The Redemptorists, however, dispute the government’s interpretation of the property’s history and say authorities have not adequately explained the legal grounds for demolishing the building. They have asked officials to publicly disclose the documentation supporting their decision and review the historical records presented by the congregation. 越南救赎主义省分会谴责了这次行动,认为当局不顾尚未解决的法律问题和一再要求审查该财产的所有权而继续行动. “正义不能通过武力建立,真理不能与被拆除的建筑物一起抹去。”

17份在拆除过程中的声明。 共产党夺地 争端集中在救赎者在1930年购买的土地上。 根据宗教秩序所引用的历史文献,胡瓦克市当局于1971年正式承认该教会的所有权. L ' Accueil建筑群后来于1938年至1943年间在地产上发展.

它作为教育、文化和社区活动中心、图书馆、礼堂和阅览室。 1950年代还在当地建立了锯木厂,提供当地就业。 1975年共产党接管南越后,政府与宗教机构的关系发生了重大变化.

全国各地的教会财产受到越来越多的国家控制,宗教社区往往失去获得其以前拥有的土地和建筑物的机会。 救赎者坚持认为,他们从未自愿放弃对L ' Accueil财产的权利。

他们承认教会在1978年将与锯木厂有关的资产转移到了国家,但辩称转让不包括土地本身. 当局随后将财产分配给政府控制的机构。 其余部分占地约2,550平方米,目前由当地体育职业学校管理.

最近的努力 自1994年以来,教会一直要求归还财产。 它最近于10月24日向胡瓦克人民委员会提出正式申诉,要求承认其土地使用权并澄清财产的法律地位。 据报告,当局在11月8日的答复中驳回了申诉,称申诉没有审议依据。

10月在该地产张贴了一份通知,宣布计划在该地开发一个公共公园和停车场. 地方当局捍卫该项目是为了公共利益,包括在人口稠密地区改善交通条件和提供更多的绿色空间。 越南法律规定,土地属于人民集体所有,由国家管理。

政府当局还援引了2003年国民议会的一项决议,该决议一般禁止重新审议1991年7月1日之前确定的某些土地和住房安排。 但救赎者质疑政府对该地产历史的解释,

他们要求官员公开公布支持其决定的文件,并审查教会提出的历史记录。 争议说明了宗教共产主义的困难

title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Meet Amid Deteriorating Religious Freedom Conditions
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperat
summary_zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京周四在中国深圳举行了一次前所未有的三方峰会，展现出合作的形象。
title_zh: 特朗普、习近平和普京在宗教自由状况恶化之际会晤
content: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperation among three of the world’s most powerful nations but offering few concrete agreements on the conflicts and international issues facing them. The roughly 80-minute meeting produced a joint statement addressing United Nations reform, energy production, international legal authority, and nuclear risks. However, the statement offered no clear breakthroughs on the wars in Ukraine or Iran and made no public reference to religious freedom or the persecution of religious communities in China and Russia. The gathering underscored the importance of direct engagement among world leaders as they seek to manage competing interests, global conflicts, and questions about the future of international order. The summit also offered an opportunity to address concerns affecting millions of people who face persecution for their faith, particularly in countries governed by authoritarian regimes. A Summit Focused on Global Stability The three leaders presented themselves as sharing responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. Their joint statement called for United Nations reform, increased production and supply of petroleum products, and further dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The leaders also emphasized state sovereignty and the immunity of government officials, declaring that the International Criminal Court and similar bodies should not abuse their authority. The language reflects a shared interest among the three governments in limiting the reach of international institutions, although their respective political, economic, and security priorities remain distinct. Concerningly, this language is similar to that used by China in pushing back on American calls to respect human rights and ensure citizens can freely practice religion. Claiming that these are internal affairs, China rejects what it considers to be overly zealous policing by the U.S. and continues on its path of persecution. Putin described the summit as a new chapter in diplomatic history and praised the opportunity for direct engagement with Trump and Xi. The Russian president also invoked the 1945 Yalta Conference, which helped shape the postwar European order, arguing that international conflicts eventually require countries to recognize realities on the ground. While the leaders expressed interest in dialogue and international stability, their meeting did not produce publicly announced agreements to resolve major conflicts or address underlying tensions between their governments. Religious Freedom Remains a Global Concern For religious freedom advocates, high-level diplomatic meetings represent an important opportunity to raise the plight of prisoners of conscience and religious communities facing government persecution. China, in particular, continues to impose severe restrictions on religious practice. Christians in unregistered churches face surveillance, detention, church closures, and pressure to submit to government oversight. The Chinese Communist Party’s campaign to bring religious institutions under its control has affected Protestant house churches, Catholic communities, Tibetan Buddhists, Uyghur Muslims, and other religious minorities. In recent months, international advocates have urged the Trump administration to raise the cases of imprisoned religious leaders with Xi. Earlier this year, Trump raised the case of Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, founder of Beijing’s Zion Church, during a meeting with Xi. Chinese authorities subsequently released Jin, who later relocated to the United States. However, other Zion Church leaders arrested during the same crackdown remain detained, and no such direct advocacy seems to have occurred at this most recent meeting. The case demonstrated how direct presidential engagement can potentially influence the circumstances
content_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但很少就它们面临的冲突和国际问题达成具体协议.

大约80分钟的会议产生了关于联合国改革、能源生产、国际法律权威和核风险的联合声明。 然而,该声明对于乌克兰或伊朗的战争没有提出明确的突破,也没有公开提及中国和俄罗斯的宗教自由或对宗教团体的迫害.

会议强调了世界领导人直接参与的重要性,因为他们寻求管理相互竞争的利益、全球冲突和有关国际秩序未来的问题。 首脑会议还提供了一个机会,解决影响到数百万因信仰而面临迫害的人的关切,特别是在专制政权统治的国家。

以全球稳定为重点的首脑会议 三位领导人自称分担维护国际和平与安全的责任。 他们的联合声明呼吁联合国改革、增加石油产品的生产和供应,以及就减少核风险进一步进行对话。

各国领导人还强调国家主权和政府官员的豁免权,宣布国际刑事法院和类似机构不应滥用其权力。 其措辞反映了三国政府对限制国际机构的影响力的共同利益,尽管它们各自的政治、经济和安全优先事项仍然不同。

关于这一点,这种语言类似于中国在抵制美国尊重人权和确保公民可以自由信奉宗教的呼声时所使用的语言。 中国声称这是内政,反对美国过于狂热地维持治安,继续走迫害的道路。

普京将峰会描述为外交史上的新篇章,并称赞与特朗普和习近平直接接触的机会. 俄罗斯总统还援引了1945年雅尔塔会议,会议帮助塑造了战后的欧洲秩序,认为国际冲突最终需要各国承认当地的实际情况.

虽然领导人对对话和国际稳定表示兴趣,但他们的会议没有达成公开宣布的协议,以解决重大冲突或解决政府之间的紧张关系。

宗教自由仍然是全球关注的问题 对于宗教自由倡导者来说,高级别外交会议是一个重要的机会,可以提高良心犯和宗教界面临政府迫害的困境。 特别是中国继续严格限制宗教活动.

在未登记的教堂的基督徒面临监视,拘留,教堂关闭,以及服从政府监督的压力. 中国共产党将宗教机构置于其控制之下的运动影响了新教住宅教堂,天主教社区,藏传佛教,维吾尔穆斯林等宗教少数派.

最近几个月,国际倡导者敦促特朗普政府向习近平提出被囚禁宗教领袖的案件. 今年早些时候,特朗普在北京锡安教会创始人伊兹拉·金明里牧师会见习近平时提出这个案例. 中国当局随后释放了后来移居美国的金.

然而,在同一次镇压中被捕的其他锡安教会领导人仍然被拘留,在最近的这次会议上似乎没有进行这种直接的宣传。 该案表明,总统直接参与会如何影响局势

title: ASEAN Continues Exclusion of Myanmar’s Military Junta Amid Ongoing Conflict
summary: Southeast Asian leaders reaffirmed their opposition to Myanmar’s military government at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila on Nov. 15, extending restrictions on the co
summary_zh: 11月15日在马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟（东盟）峰会上，东南亚各国领导人重申了他们对缅甸军政府的反对立场，并延长了对该国领导人参加东盟会议的限制。
title_zh: 在持续冲突的背景下，东盟继续将缅甸军政府排除在外
content: Southeast Asian leaders reaffirmed their opposition to Myanmar’s military government at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila on Nov. 15, extending restrictions on the country’s political representation after concluding that its military leadership had made insufficient progress toward ending the country’s civil war. The decision came as leaders from the 11-member regional bloc gathered in the Philippines for three days of discussions on international conflicts, regional security, and economic stability. Myanmar’s continuing violence and humanitarian crisis featured prominently, alongside disputes in the South China Sea and the broader consequences of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. In a statement following their review of Myanmar’s implementation of a five-point peace plan adopted in 2021, ASEAN leaders expressed deep concern over the continuing conflict. They denounced attacks against civilians and public infrastructure. They called on all parties to halt indiscriminate violence, protect civilian populations, and allow humanitarian assistance to reach those in need. The leaders also agreed to maintain the restriction preventing Myanmar’s military leader and foreign minister from attending ASEAN summits and foreign ministers’ meetings until meaningful progress is made toward implementing the peace plan. Myanmar will continue to be represented at those meetings by lower-level diplomatic officials. The decision represents a positive continuation of ASEAN’s effort to pressure Myanmar’s military leadership while preserving diplomatic channels with the country. A Peace Plan with Little Progress Myanmar has been embroiled in a nationwide civil war since February 2021, when the military overthrew the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi. The coup prompted widespread protests and a violent crackdown by security forces. Armed resistance subsequently emerged across the country, with longstanding ethnic armed organizations also intensifying their campaigns against the military. In April 2021, ASEAN developed a five-point consensus intended to address the crisis. The agreement called for an immediate cessation of violence, constructive dialogue among all parties, mediation by an ASEAN special envoy, humanitarian assistance, and engagement between the envoy and relevant stakeholders. Despite repeated diplomatic efforts, the plan has produced little meaningful progress toward ending the conflict. ASEAN has struggled to balance its traditional policy of noninterference in member states’ domestic affairs with the need to respond to the increasingly severe humanitarian and political crisis in Myanmar. The bloc has maintained contact with the military government while withholding full political recognition at its highest-level meetings. In May 2025, ASEAN attempted to strengthen its approach by making the special envoy position permanent rather than replacing the representative annually. The change was intended to provide greater continuity in diplomatic engagement and improve the prospects for negotiations. However, continued military operations and widespread abuses have undermined those efforts. According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent monitoring organization, more than 8,600 people had been killed and 32,406 arrested by Myanmar’s security forces as of this week. The figures reflect the extensive human cost of the conflict and the government’s continued repression of opposition. Myanmar’s military leadership has also attempted to restore its international standing. Military chief Min Aung Hlaing became president in April following elections conducted in phases in December and January. Opposition groups and international observers criticized the elections as an effort to consolidate military control rather than restore genuine civilian government. Despite visits to several ASEAN member states, Min Aung Hlaing remains excluded from the bloc’s highest-level politi
content_zh:
东南亚领导人在11月15日于马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟(东盟)首脑会议上重申反对缅甸军政府,认为缅甸的军事领导在结束该国内战方面进展不足后,延长了对该国政治代表权的限制.

这项决定是11个成员的区域集团领导人在菲律宾聚集一堂,讨论国际冲突、区域安全和经济稳定问题,为期三天。 缅甸的持续暴力和人道主义危机与南中国海的争端以及中东和乌克兰冲突的更广泛后果一道,占据了显著地位。

东盟领导人在审查缅甸执行2021年通过的五点和平计划后发表声明,对持续冲突深表关切. 他们谴责对平民和公共基础设施的袭击。 他们呼吁所有各方停止不分青红皂白的暴力,保护平民,允许人道主义援助送达需要援助的人。

领导人还同意继续限制缅甸的军事领导人和外交部长出席东盟首脑会议和外交部长会议,直到在执行和平计划方面取得有意义的进展。 缅甸将继续派低级外交官员出席这些会议。

这一决定是东盟在保持与缅甸的外交渠道的同时向缅甸军事领导人施压的努力的积极继续。 自2021年2月军方推翻昂山素季当选政府以来,与小进步缅甸的和平计划卷入全国内战.

政变引发了广泛的抗议和安全部队的暴力镇压. 武装抵抗随后在全国各地出现,长期存在的族裔武装组织也加强了对军队的进攻。 2021年4月,东盟达成了旨在应对危机的五点共识.

协定要求立即停止暴力,所有各方进行建设性对话,由东盟特使进行调解,提供人道主义援助,特使与相关利益攸关方进行接触。 尽管一再作出外交努力,但该计划在结束冲突方面没有取得什么有意义的进展。

东盟努力在不干涉成员国内政的传统政策与应对缅甸日益严重的人道主义和政治危机的必要性之间取得平衡。 该集团与军政府保持联系,同时拒绝在最高级别会议上给予充分的政治承认。

2025年5月,东盟试图加强其做法,使特使的职位永久化,而不是每年更换代表。 这一变化旨在增加外交接触的连续性,改善谈判前景。 然而,持续的军事行动和普遍的侵权行为破坏了这些努力。

据独立监督组织政治犯援助协会称,截至本周,缅甸安全部队已杀害8 600多人,逮捕32 406人。 这些数字反映了冲突给人带来的巨大代价以及政府继续镇压反对派。

缅甸的军事领导人也试图恢复其国际地位。 在12月和1月分阶段举行选举之后,军事长官敏昂·赫莱于4月成为总统。 反对派团体和国际观察员批评选举是为了巩固军事控制而不是恢复真正的文职政府。

尽管访问了东盟的几个成员国,敏昂莱仍然被排除在集团最高领导层之外。

title: Fulani Militants Kill 14 Christians in Plateau State, Nigeria
summary: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure
summary_zh: 在尼日利亚博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统就其未能保护人民免受袭击一事呼吁原谅的几天后，在高原州的四个地方政府辖区内发生的最新袭击中，至少有14名基督徒被杀害。
title_zh: 富拉尼武装分子在尼日利亚高原州杀害14名基督徒
content: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure to visit violence-affected communities during an earlier trip to the state and promised to rebuild destroyed communities and return internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes. The killings occurred between Sunday, Nov. 15, and Monday, Nov. 16, in Mangu, Riyom, Barkin Ladi and Bokkos local government areas, according to community sources and local security groups. Armed attackers reportedly targeted rural settlements and ambushed residents traveling between communities. The latest violence followed Tinubu’s visit to Jos on Saturday, Nov. 14, for an All Progressives Congress (APC) political rally at Zaria Road Stadium, where he acknowledged the suffering of communities affected by recurring attacks and displacement. Addressing residents and party supporters, Tinubu asked Plateau residents to forgive him for not visiting affected communities during his previous trip to the state in April. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport,” he said. “Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation. I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people.” The president promised to rebuild communities destroyed by violence and facilitate the return of displaced residents. “We will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your communities,” Tinbu added. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau.” He also commended the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr. Bernard Doro, for identifying vulnerable populations and coordinating humanitarian assistance. Tinubu announced that 1,000 forest guards were undergoing training and that surveillance cameras promised to Plateau state had been procured to strengthen security monitoring and early warning operations. However, fresh attacks were reported within hours of the president’s departure from the state. In Mangu Local Government Area, armed attackers invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, killing nine people. Other residents were reportedly missing following the attack. Silas Nanfwang, a resident who confirmed the incident to journalists, called on security agencies to intensify efforts to locate the attackers and bring those responsible to justice. In Barkin Ladi, 79-year-old Da Ishaku Pam Vwos was killed when armed men invaded Sho village at about 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, according to the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM). The association’s National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, also reported the killing of 42-year-old Dauda John Davou during an attack on the Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, at about 2 a.m. on Sunday. Another attack was reported in the Jol community around 12:10 a.m. on Sunday. According to BYM, local vigilantes responded to the attackers, preventing further casualties. The association said the incidents followed the shooting of Joshua Doro Dafwel in Jol on Wednesday. He is currently receiving medical attention. BYM also reported that Ina Arin was killed when armed men ambushed him and his friend, Abok Gyang, as they returned to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang survived the attack. In Bokkos Local Government Area, two people, including a unit commander of the Plateau state-owned security outfit, Operation Rainbow, were killed in an ambush on Monday afternoon. The victims, identified as Gambo and his companion, were traveling on a motorcycle from Hurti village to Tadai in Manguna District when armed men attacked them at about 1:30 p.m. They had reportedly visited Hurti for a condolence visit and died at the scene. Gambo had recently completed a refresher training program for Operation Rainbow unit commanders in Jos and was known amon
content_zh:
在博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统呼吁原谅他在早些时候访问受暴力影响的社区,并承诺重建被摧毁的社区并让境内流离失所者返回其祖传家园几天后,在尼日利亚高原州四个地方政府地区,至少有14名基督徒被杀死。

据社区人士和地方安全团体称,这些杀戮发生在11月15日星期日至16日星期一的Mangu、Riyom、Barkin Ladi和Bokkos地方政府地区。 据报告,武装袭击者以农村定居点为目标,并伏击社区之间的居民。 在Tinubu于11月星期六访问Jos后,

14,在Zaria Road体育场举行全体进步人士大会(APC)政治集会,他承认一再受攻击和流离失所影响的社区遭受苦难。 蒂努布针对居民和政党支持者,要求高原居民原谅他4月前去该州旅行期间没有访问受影响的社区.

他说,“上次访问时,我仅限于机场。” “对不起,如果你没有在内地看到我,但我看到了灾难。 我收到州长的报告了 我在我国人民的脸上看到了恐怖。” 总统承诺重建被暴力摧毁的社区并便利流离失所居民回返。

Tinbu补充说,“我们将重建你们的社区,并将你们带回你们的社区。” “我已指示所有安全机构采取果断行动,并维持高原的和平与稳定。” 他还赞扬人道主义事务和减贫部长贝尔纳·多罗博士确定弱势人口和协调人道主义援助。

蒂努布宣布有1000名森林警卫正在接受训练,并且已经采购了向高原州承诺的监视相机,以加强安全监测和预警行动. 然而,据报道,总统离开国家后的数小时内又有新的袭击.

在Mangu地方政府地区,武装袭击者于星期日下午9时左右入侵Jipal区的Zwagal社区,造成9人死亡。 据报告,其他居民在袭击后失踪。 向记者证实此事的居民Silas Nanfwang呼吁安全机构加紧努力找到袭击者,并将责任人绳之以法。

在Barkin Ladi,79岁的Da Ishaku Pam Vwos被武装分子于星期日下午5:20左右入侵Sho村而死,据Berom青年穆尔德斯协会(BYM)称. 该协会的全国宣传秘书Rwang Tengwong还报道了42岁的Dauda John Davou星期天凌晨2时左右在Riyom LGA的Hoss区被Sambak社区袭击时被杀死的事件。

据报道,乔尔社区在星期日12:10左右又发生了一起袭击事件. 据BYM称,当地民团对袭击者作出反应,防止了进一步的伤亡. 该协会说,事件发生在周三Joshua Doro Dafwel被枪击后。 他目前正在接受治疗。

受害者被确认为Gambo和他的同伴,他们乘坐摩托车从Hurti村前往Manguna区的Tadai,武装人员于下午1时30分左右袭击他们。 据报告,他们前往Hurti慰问,并在现场死亡。 甘博最近完成了 " 彩虹行动 " 部队指挥官在乔斯的进修培训方案,并被称作 " 阿蒙 "

title: Hindu Nationalists Target Christians in West Bengal, India
summary: At least 48 to 65 incidents of targeted harassment, church vandalism, and physical violence against Christian communities in West Bengal, India, have been recorded between May and November. The Bangiy
summary_zh: 据记录，5月至11月期间，印度西孟加拉邦发生了至少48至65起针对性骚扰、破坏教堂和针对基督徒社区的暴力行为。
title_zh: 印度西孟加拉邦的印度教民族主义者将矛头对准基督徒
content: At least 48 to 65 incidents of targeted harassment, church vandalism, and physical violence against Christian communities in West Bengal, India, have been recorded between May and November. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba, a Christian organization working for the welfare of the state’s Christian community, compiled this data. The right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in West Bengal following the April 2026 Legislative Assembly elections. Independent tracking by the research group India Hate Lab verified 60 hate crime incidents explicitly targeting Christian individuals, domestic fellowships, and institutional properties within West Bengal during the same period, confirming the widespread geographic footprint of the escalation of attacks on Christians. According to reports, the latest attack occurred on Nov. 9, when vandals desecrated a sacred shrine and Marian grotto of a church in an overnight attack in Khari Bamuner Chak, located within the Raidighi and Baruipur pastoral region of West Bengal’s South Parganas. A week earlier, a heavily organized contingent of about 40 men attacked a house prayer fellowship in Rayan village of the Bardhaman area. The assailants stormed the private residence during a morning service, violently assaulting the officiating pastor and worshippers. Surge of Attacks The surge in targeted violence, intimidation, and vandalism against Christian communities, churches, and home prayer fellowships in West Bengal is proving that Hindu nationalists have found West Bengal to be the new hunting ground with tacit support of the authorities. The state is currently experiencing a rapid breakdown in local law enforcement deterrence. This erosion directly threatens the constitutional guarantees enshrined in Article 25 of the Indian Constitution, which ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion. The emergence of organized Hindutva networks operating with near-total impunity represents not merely localized social friction, but a systemic challenge to the rule of law and civil stability across the state. Faith Space Shrinking Across rural and semi-urban districts of West Bengal, Hindu nationalists increasingly employ physical blockades, structural desecration, and coordinated mob actions to shrink the space for religious minority assemblies. By weaponizing social intimidation and exploiting police inertia, these actors seek to criminalize ordinary acts of devotion, transforming private exercise of faith into contested public security triggers. Detailed documentation by human rights organizations and community defense networks attributes the vast majority of these incursions to organized Hindutva-affiliated groups. Investigations specifically point to operational coordination by local cadres associated with the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and the Bajrang Dal, the RSS’s militant arm. Assailants consistently deploy dual narratives of illegal “unlawful religious conversions” and fabricated “honey traps.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . content_zh:
5月至11月期间,印度西孟加拉邦至少有48至65起针对基督教社区的有针对性骚扰、破坏教堂和人身暴力事件。 Bangiya Christiya Pariseba是一个致力于国家基督教团体福利的基督教组织,

右翼印度民族主义者Bharatiya Janata党(BJP)于2026年4月立法议会选举后在西孟加拉邦上台.

研究小组印度仇恨实验室的独立跟踪核实了同期60起仇恨犯罪事件,明确针对西孟加拉邦的基督教个人、家庭奖学金和机构财产,证实了对基督教徒袭击升级造成的广泛地域影响。 据报道,最近一次袭击发生在11月.

9日,在位于西孟加拉邦南帕尔干纳斯的Raigighi和Baruipur牧区Khari Bamuner Chak的一起夜间袭击中,被破坏者亵渎了一座圣地和一座教堂的Marian地道。 一周前,一支由约40名男子组成的组织严密的特遣队袭击了Bardhaman地区Rayan村的一个家庭祈祷研究金。

袭击者在上午礼拜时冲入了私人住宅,暴力袭击了牧师和礼拜者。

袭击的激增 西孟加拉邦针对基督教社区、教堂和家庭祈祷研究金的有针对性暴力、恐吓和破坏行为激增,证明印度教民族主义者在当局的默许下发现西孟加拉邦是新的狩猎地。 目前,该国地方执法威慑迅速崩溃。

这种削弱直接威胁到《印度宪法》第25条所载的宪法保障,该条确保良心自由和自由信奉、实践和传播宗教的权利。

有组织的印度人网络的出现几乎完全不受惩罚,这不仅是局部性的社会摩擦,而且是对全国法治和国内稳定的系统性挑战。

印度民族主义者在西孟加拉邦的农村和半城市地区越来越多地采取实际封锁、结构性亵渎、协调暴徒行动来缩小宗教少数群体集会的空间。

通过将社会恐吓武器化和利用警察惯性,这些行为者试图将普通的献身行为定为刑事犯罪,将个人信仰的行使转变为有争议的公共安全触发因素。 人权组织和社区防卫网络的详细文件将绝大多数入侵归因于有组织的印度教附属团体。

调查特别指向与印度印度人理事会(VHP)和RSS好战武装Bajrang Dal有关的当地干部的业务协调。 仆从们一贯使用非法的“非法宗教皈依”和捏造的“甜蜜陷阱”的双重说法。 更多新闻报导, 采访,请通过电子邮件。

title_zh: 马来西亚法院将一名皈依基督教者的宗教自由诉讼移交地区法庭
content: A 34-year-old law graduate’s multi-year battle exposes the severe reality of religious control and the legal trap facing citizens who want to leave Islam. A high-stakes constitutional challenge highlighting the erosion of religious freedom in Malaysia has taken a procedural step backward. The Kuala Lumpur High Court has ordered that a lawsuit filed by a 34-year-old legal researcher seeking legal recognition as a Christian be transferred to the Shah Alam High Court. The case lays bare the rigid and intrusive control exercised by state apparatuses and Islamic religious authorities over personal faith, showcasing a system where basic human rights — such as choosing one’s own religion — are tightly policed by the government. A Life Labeled Without Consent The plaintiff, Shameer PV, identifies as a Christian and has lived as one since he was 18. However, under strict Malaysian administrative regulations, the word “Islam” was stamped on his compulsory national identity card (MyKad) when he was just 12, following a bureaucratic policy introduced under the National Registration Act. Despite decades of personal conviction and his marriage to a Christian wife, the state continues to legally treat him as a Muslim, directly violating his parental and marital status and refusing to recognize his family. Shameer’s legal challenge names the federal government, the Selangor state government, and the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) as defendants. He argues that labeling citizens by religion on state identity cards violates Article 11(1) of the Federal Constitution, which ostensibly guarantees every person the right to profess and practice their religion. Trapped in Shariah Bureaucracy Shameer’s ordeal underscores the labyrinthine and punishing hurdles forced upon religious minorities and converts in Malaysia’s dual-justice system, which runs a parallel set of Islamic (Shariah) courts alongside the civil judiciary. In 2018, Shameer initiated proceedings in a Selangor Shariah court seeking official recognition of his Christian faith. After an exhausting 72 court sessions spanning over seven years, the Shariah court dismissed his application in January. Rather than allowing him to move on with his life, the religious court went a step further, ordering state departments and Islamic authorities to “guide and control” his practice of Islam — effectively treating his desire to leave the faith as a disciplinary or correctional matter. Having exhausted the religious tribunal system, Shameer turned to the civil high court in July, filing an originating summons to ask the highest judicial authorities whether state-mandated religious labeling on identity cards is unconstitutional, and whether Shariah courts have any lawful jurisdiction over individuals who do not practice Islam. A Wider Crisis for Freedom of Conscience International human rights observers and religious freedom advocates have long criticized Malaysia’s legal framework regarding apostasy and conversion. While the Malaysian Constitution theoretically protects freedom of religion, civil courts have repeatedly ruled that only Islamic Shariah courts have the authority to permit someone to leave Islam — creating an effective judicial catch-22, as Shariah courts rarely grant permission to renounce the religion. For international human rights advocates and supporters of religious liberty, Shameer’s case is a stark reminder of the state-enforced religious controls facing millions in Southeast Asia. As his case moves to the Shah Alam court, the legal battle continues to test whether Malaysia’s secular constitutional framework can protect an individual’s fundamental right of conscience against a totalizing state religious bureaucracy. content_zh:
一个34岁的法学毕业生的多年战斗暴露了宗教控制的严重现实和想要离开伊斯兰教的公民所面临的法律陷阱. 马来西亚宗教自由受到侵蚀,

吉隆坡高等法院下令将34岁法律研究者提出的寻求法律承认为基督徒的诉讼移交沙阿拉姆高等法院.

这一案件暴露了国家机构和伊斯兰宗教当局对个人信仰的严格和侵扰性控制,表明政府严格控制基本人权(如选择自己的宗教)的制度。 未经同意的生活标签 原告Shameer PV确认为基督教徒,自18岁起就一直作为一个教徒生活在一起。

然而,根据严格的马来西亚行政条例,他12岁时的强制性国民身份证(MyKad)上印有“伊斯兰”一词,这是根据《国家登记法》实行的官僚政策。

尽管几十年的个人信念和他与基督教妻子的婚姻,但国家继续在法律上将他视为穆斯林,直接侵犯了他的父母和婚姻状况,并拒绝承认他的家人. 沙门的法律质疑将联邦政府,雪兰莪州政府,雪兰莪伊斯兰宗教委员会(MAIS)列为被告.

他辩称,以宗教方式将公民贴在州身份证上违反了《联邦宪法》第11(1)条,该条表面上保障每个人信奉和奉行其宗教的权利。

伊斯兰教法官僚沙姆耶的折磨凸显了Labyrinthine和惩罚强加给宗教少数派和皈依马来西亚双重司法制度的障碍,马来西亚的双重司法制度与民事司法平行设有一套伊斯兰(伊斯兰教法)法院。 2018年,沙姆耶在塞兰哥教法法院提起诉讼,寻求官方承认他的基督教信仰.

经过历时七年的72次开庭,教法法院于1月驳回了他的申请。

宗教法庭没有让他继续自己的生活,而是更进一步,命令国家部门和伊斯兰当局“指导和控制”他的伊斯兰教习俗——实际上将他放弃信仰的愿望视为纪律或惩戒事项。

在用尽了宗教法庭制度之后,Shameer于7月向民事高等法院提交了原传票,询问最高司法当局在身份证上贴上国家规定的宗教标签是否违宪,伊斯兰教法法院是否对不信奉伊斯兰教的个人拥有任何合法管辖权。

国际人权观察员和宗教自由倡导者长期批评马来西亚关于叛教和皈依的法律框架。

虽然马来西亚宪法理论上保护宗教自由,但民事法院一再裁定只有伊斯兰教法法院有权允许某人离开伊斯兰教——这创造了有效的司法抓捕-22,因为伊斯兰教法法院很少允许放弃该宗教.

对国际人权倡导者和宗教自由支持者来说,Shameer一案明确提醒人们注意东南亚数百万人所面临的国家强制宗教控制。

summary_zh: 11月1日，六人在被富拉尼族极端分子关押超过六个月后，迈出了重获自由的第一步。其中一人仅两天后就去世了。13岁的哈萨娜·布卢斯（Hasana Bulus）在被送往医院时已处于危急状态，后在医院去世。布卢斯是富拉尼民兵绑架的11人之一……   这篇题为《少女被囚禁六个月后死亡》的文章最初发表在“国际基督徒关注”网站上。
title_zh: 少女被囚禁六个月后死亡
content: On Nov. 1, six people took their first steps of freedom after being held by Fulani extremists for more than six months. One of them died only two days later. Hasana Bulus, 13, died in the hospital where she was taken in critical condition. Bulus was one of the 11 people who were kidnapped by a Fulani militia in April. One had escaped, but five died at the camp, and the rest were released with Bulus — including the 4-year-old daughter of a woman who had died in captivity. Bulus’ village, Awon, is predominantly Christian and has been the target of Fulani attacks, just like Ariko, a neighboring village in Kaduna state. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. Ariko is home to the 37 Christians who were kidnapped during the Easter services earlier this year in a neighboring village. Of these, 17 people have died in captivity, 12 have escaped, and eight have since been released. The abductees from both these villages were held in the same forest hideout, where they were kept in inhumane conditions. “They [the villagers] told us how they would stay for two weeks without food,” one woman, whose father died in the camp, told Open Doors . “They only boil water to drink. That’s how they struggled before the bandits gave them corn flour, and they started making swallow (a porridge). The men are restrained, chained in groups; they are not free to move around.” All of the male abductees in these groups had died in the camp. Christian Solidarity Worldwide (CSW) is calling for Nigerian authorities to protect these communities and fight to free more people left in bondage. “We continue to urge the Nigerian government at state and federal levels to prioritize the protection of vulnerable communities throughout the nation, to combat the threat posed by the litany of terrorist groups that are active in the country far more effectively, and to secure the release of all abductees,” CSW CEO Scot Bower said. “Nigeria’s Christians do not need another statement of sympathy,” ICC’s president, Shawn Wright, said. “They need protection , justice , and accountability . When those who murder innocent Christians face no meaningful consequences, impunity becomes an invitation to the next attack. The Nigerian government must protect vulnerable communities, pursue the perpetrators, and make clear that these crimes will not go unanswered.” Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . 1人逃跑了,但5人死于营地,其余的人与布卢斯一起被释放——包括一名在囚禁中死亡的妇女的4岁女儿. 与卡杜纳州邻近村庄阿里科一样,

根据非洲宗教自由观察站(ORFA)进行的一项为期六年的研究,伊斯兰富拉尼民兵是尼日利亚基督教徒最致命的迫害者。 阿里科是37名基督徒的家,他们在今年早些时候在复活节礼拜期间在一个邻近村庄被绑架。

其中,17人在囚禁中死亡,12人逃脱,8人自此获释. 这两个村庄的被绑架者被关在同一个森林藏身处,他们被关在不人道的条件下。 “他们[村民]告诉我们,他们将如何在没有食物的情况下呆两周,”一位父亲死于营地的妇女告诉Open Doors。 “他们只煮水饮用。

在土匪给他们面粉之前, 这些人被捆绑起来,被捆绑在一起;他们不能自由移动。” 这些团伙中的所有男性被绑架者都死于营地。

世界基督教团结会呼吁尼日利亚当局保护这些社区,并努力释放更多受奴役的人。

“我们继续敦促尼日利亚州和联邦政府优先保护全国的弱势社区,更有效地打击在该国活动的众多恐怖主义团体构成的威胁,并确保释放所有被绑架者。”

“尼日利亚的基督徒不需要再次表示同情, “他们需要保护、正义和问责制。 当杀害无辜基督徒的人没有面临有意义的后果时,有罪不罚就成为下一次袭击的诱因。

summary_zh:
据报告,11月10日,民主同盟军伊斯兰叛乱分子在刚果东北部伊图里省曼巴萨县发动了新的袭击,造成26人死亡,另有数人被绑架,该国近93%的人口是基督教徒。

title_zh: 刚果民主共和国曼巴萨地区在埃博拉疫情期间至少有26人死亡
content: Twenty-six people have reportedly been killed and several others abducted in a new attack carried out by the Islamist rebels of Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on Nov. 10, during the night, in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, northeastern DR Congo, a country where nearly 93% of the population is Christian. According to a local association coordinator, Malikidogo, more than six villages were affected, including Kangwayi, Misele, Mingazi, and Mambaka. “The situation is very serious; we identified 26 people killed, several others abducted, and many families are still searching for their missing loved ones,” Malikidogo said. “Aside from the death of many people, five houses were burnt alongside some motorcycles. We are calling on the authorities to take urgent action to protect the population.” Left With Nothing Survivors who succeeded in escaping reported that many families had to run for their lives, leaving their homes and belongings behind. “We were very afraid when we realized that the enemies were already in the village when we heard people crying and others running in every direction,” one survivor said. “We just fled without having time to collect our belongings, just to save our lives. We do not know what will happen next, and we are afraid that they might come and reach Mambasa city where we are today.” The attack comes at a difficult time for local communities, which are already facing the threat of Ebola . Residents are now dealing with both the fear of the disease and the danger of further attacks. There are concerns that the violence could also make it harder to control the Ebola outbreak. People fleeing their villages may spread the disease to other communities, while insecurity could prevent health workers from reaching those who need medical help. A local leader also expressed concern about the situation and called for stronger protection of civilians. “We have suffered for many years because of the atrocities committed by ADF Islamist terrorists,” he said. “We are already struggling with Ebola, and now we are facing these attacks again. We cannot continue living like this. We are calling on the government and security forces to protect our communities before more innocent lives are lost.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . The post At Least 26 Killed in DRC’s Mambasa Territory Amid Ebola Crisis first appeared on International Christian Concern .
content_zh:
据报告,11月10日,民主同盟军伊斯兰叛乱分子在刚果东北部伊图里省曼巴萨县发动了新的袭击,造成26人死亡,另有数人被绑架,该国近93%的人口是基督教徒。

据当地协会协调员Malikidogo说,有6个以上的村庄受到影响,其中包括Kangwayi、Misele、Mingazi和Mambaka。 “局势非常严重;我们确认有26人被杀害,另有数人被绑架,许多家庭仍在寻找失踪的亲人。”

“除了许多人的死亡外,还有五所房屋与一些摩托车一起被烧毁。 我们呼吁当局采取紧急行动保护人民。” 成功逃脱的幸存者一无所有地离开,报告说,许多家庭不得不逃命,留下家园和财物。

一位幸存者说,“当我们意识到敌人已经在村里时,我们非常害怕,当我们听到人们在哭,而其他人则朝每个方向奔跑时”。 “我们刚刚逃离,没有时间收集我们的财产,只是为了拯救我们的生命。

我们不知道接下来会发生什么,我们担心他们会来到我们今天所在的曼巴萨市。” 袭击发生在当地社区面临埃博拉威胁的困难时刻。 居民们现在正在处理对疾病的恐惧和进一步攻击的危险。

人们担心暴力也可能使控制埃博拉疫情变得更加困难。 逃离村庄的人可能把这种疾病传播到其他社区,而不安全则可能妨碍保健工作者帮助需要医疗帮助的人。 一名当地领导人还对局势表示关切,呼吁加强对平民的保护。

他说,“由于民主同盟军伊斯兰恐怖分子的暴行,我们受苦多年。” “我们已经在与埃博拉作斗争,现在我们再次面临这些袭击。 我们不能继续这样生活。 我们要求政府和安全部队在更多的无辜者丧生之前保护我们的社区。” 阅读更多新闻,

请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作, 至少26人在刚果民主共和国曼巴萨领地死于埃博拉危机,
author: commsmanager

title: A Maker’s Heart
source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
summary: Holly Neal turned a lifelong love of creating into an unexpected opportunity to support sign language Bible translation.   The post  A Maker’s Heart  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
summary_zh: 霍莉·尼尔（Holly Neal）将自己毕生对创作的热爱化为支持手语圣经翻译的意外机会。   这篇题为《创作者的心》的文章  最初发表在  Wycliffe 上。
title_zh: 创作者的心
content: Holly Neal loves people, and she loves making things. And when something catches her interest, she dives in. “I’m a maker,” she said simply. But making has become more than just a hobby for Holly. Through some of her family’s hardest seasons, it has offered them comfort and connection. And eventually it became an unexpected way to give back to what God is doing around the world. When Holly’s adult daughter Julia was being treated for leukemia, a friend invited them to learn how to quilt. The creative process gave Holly something to focus on as their family walked through a difficult season. It became a way to work through hard things alongside her daughter. Years later, when Holly’s grandson Graham was born during the COVID-19 pandemic, she reached for another familiar project: cross-stitching. Graham spent his first four months in the hospital. And because of visitation restrictions at the time, Holly spent long hours waiting in the cafeteria. So she brought her cross-stitch. Being busy helped calm Holly’s mind. Cross-stitching was a small, practical way to make the waiting a little easier. Holly and her husband, Steve, have continued to navigate some unique family circumstances as they’ve cared for their daughter and grandson. So when Chris and Lindsay Beals, Holly and Steven’s daughter and son-in-law, invited the couple to a Wycliffe event, they were especially excited. After a season of isolation, they looked forward to reconnecting with other Christians and hearing stories about what God was doing through Bible translation. One part of the work specifically stayed with Holly: sign language Bible translation. Curious about what sign language Bible translation actually looks like? See for yourself when you visit our interactive Bible Translation Experience! You’ll go on a global journey where you’ll meet some of the hardworking Deaf translators bringing the Bible to their people in a language and format that capture their hearts. Start your journey! → As a grandmother of a child with unique needs, Holly has a special place in her heart for communities and families who navigate specific challenges and contexts. Learning about the work of making God’s Word accessible to Deaf communities worldwide gave Holly a personal connection to a ministry she’d never fully understood before. Holly and Steve had already talked and prayed about a financial gift they wanted to make to Wycliffe. But as she continued thinking about the ministry and Bible translation projects for sign languages, another question kept coming to mind: “Steve and I had already come up with a number that we felt like to donate, but the Lord kept speaking to me. And I kept thinking, ‘But what can I do? … That’s our money, but how can I make an impact?’” So Holly began thinking about how much she had invested — in supplies, patterns, fabric and tools — over the years in her love of crafting. She wondered if some of those things could become part of her gift to Bible translation. And what if Holly passed some of those supplies along to other makers and used the proceeds to support Bible translation for sign languages? See how one couple in Alabama also creatively used their gifts and skills to give back to Bible translation → Giving in Community Holly decided to hold what the stitching community calls a “destash” — an opportunity for her to sell supplies she already owned to other stitchers who could put them to good use. She shared the idea through her YouTube channel and social media, where she had already connected with a community of people who love cross-stitch. So when Holly told her stitching community about Wycliffe and her desire to support sign language Bible translation, she invited them into partnering with something that mattered to her. And people responded with generosity! Some people paid more for supplies and projects than the asking price, wanting to give a little extra toward the cause. title_zh: 管教孩子的内心（与Melissa Paredes的谈话）
content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. title: Living Out a Legacy of Stewardship and Faith

summary: Ken and Sally discovered a way to give God’s Word — a gift they’d had access to their whole lives — to others.    The post  Living Out a Legacy of Stewardship and Faith  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
summary_zh: Ken和Sally发现了一种方法，可以将上帝的话语--这是他们一生都能接触到的礼物--传递给他人。“活出管理和信仰的遗产”一文首次出现在威克里夫。
title_zh: 活出管理和信仰的遗产
content: What did your journey to faith look like? Perhaps it was a story of how God showed up in the midst of uncertainty, doubt or fears. Maybe it involved Him seeking you out and rescuing you. Or maybe you grew up in a Christian household and your story is a bit different — perhaps your family regularly read the Bible together and have always known about Jesus’ love. Ken Trager was raised that way. He reflected, “I think when you’re raised in a Christian home … and you have the routines of a life that is built around church and prayer, you just take it for granted.” He added, “It was just the air I breathed.” For Ken and his wife, Sally, faith was always part of their stories. They were each raised in Christian homes, followed Christ, got baptized and had parents who faithfully modeled church attendance, prayer and generosity.  Ken and Sally’s paths eventually crossed at Greenville University in southern Illinois, where they met and fell in love. They went on to build a life centered around family, faith and service. Ken spent his career as a teacher and coach while Sally worked as an accountant, and together they raised two children. Now retired, they’ve moved to be closer to their children and grandchildren, giving them a new opportunity to pour into the next generation. Through all those years and seasons, the faith Ken and Sally had seen modeled by their families continued to shape their home. Early in their marriage, Ken and Sally met a mentor who encouraged the couple to go deeper with their faith — to study Scripture, ask questions and wrestle honestly with what they believed. It was an important season of discovering that the faith that had been passed down from their families could also become something they personally owned and lived out together. What Do You Take for Granted? Years later, the couple experienced an aha moment when they were introduced to Wycliffe at an event. There, Ken and Sally heard story after story from people who had received Scripture in their own languages. Something clicked for Sally: “We’ve never known a day where we couldn’t access the Bible. And these people have just longed for it, and they’re finally getting it.” For the first time, something that had always surrounded the couple became visible — and it was a gift they could no longer take for granted . Ken and Sally had spent years thinking about the importance of God’s Word. Seeing people receive Scripture in their own languages helped them understand just how extraordinary that access is. “The power of salvation comes through that,” Ken said. “I can’t think of … [a more] important work than providing God’s Word to everybody in the world.” Sally agreed. “To have His Word is as if we’re hearing the voice of God,” she said. “God works through His Word.” This conviction — for people around the world to be able to access Scripture for themselves — became one of the reasons Ken and Sally prioritized a place in their giving for Wycliffe. But it also became part of a larger question about generosity they had been asking themselves for years: “If everything we have is a gift from God, what does it look like to live generously with it?” A Generous Heart Generosity, like faith, was something Ken and Sally had grown up around. Ken remembers his dad giving him money to put in the offering plate, and Sally remembers watching her parents give not just to their church but to people and organizations in need. Sally’s father especially enjoyed giving anonymously. As Ken and Sally have grown older, they’ve learned that generosity isn’t simply about giving a certain percentage or checking a box; it’s about continually asking what it means to have a generous heart . For Ken, the question of what it means to be generous has become what he calls “Kingdom Advancement Giving.” When contemplating giving, he asks, “Is this going to advance the Kingdom for God’s glory?” That question has shaped the way the couple thinks about which individuals and organizations they

他回想道 , “ 我想当你在基督教家庭长大... 你有一个在教堂和祷告周围建造的日常生活, 你只是把它视为理所当然。 ” 他又说:“只是我呼吸的空气。” 对于肯和他的妻子莎莉来说,信仰总是他们的故事的一部分.

他们各自在基督教家中长大,跟随基督,接受洗礼,并有忠实的模范教会出席,祈祷和慷慨的父母. 肯和莎莉的道路最终在伊利诺伊州南部的格林维尔大学交叉,在那里他们相遇并坠入爱河. 他们继续建立一个以家庭、信仰和服务为中心的生活。

肯在萨利担任会计期间度过了教师和教练的生涯,两人一起抚养两个孩子. 他们已经退休了, 他们已经搬到更亲近他们的儿孙, 给他们一个新的机会, 注入下一代。 在那些年和季节中,肯和莎莉所见到的由家人塑造的信仰继续塑造自己的家园.

早年的婚姻中,肯和莎莉结识了一位导师,他鼓励这对夫妇更深入地信仰——学习圣经,提出问题,并诚实地与所相信的东西搏斗. 这是一个重要的季节,发现从家人传下来的信仰也可能成为他们个人拥有和共同生活的东西. 你拿什么给格兰特?

多年后,夫妇俩在一次活动上被介绍到怀克利夫(Wycliffe)时,经历了一段愉快的时刻. 在那里,肯和莎莉从以自己语言接受圣经的人那里听到一个接一个的故事. “我们从未知道有一天我们无法阅读圣经。

而这些人也只是渴望, 第一次,一直包围着这对夫妇的东西变得明显——这是他们不能再视为理所当然的礼物了. 肯和莎莉花了多年时间思考上帝之言的重要性.

看到人们用自己的语言接受圣经 有助于他们理解这种访问是多么非凡 肯说,“救赎的力量来自此”。 " 我无法想象......比向全世界每个人提供上帝的话更重要的工作。 " 萨莉同意了 ”她说,

“真主通过他的话而工作。” 这种信念——让世界各地的人们能够为自己获得圣经——成为肯和莎莉在为威克利夫奉献一个位置时优先考虑的原因之一.

但是,它也成为了一个更大的问题的一部分,即他们多年来一直问自己:“如果我们所拥有的一切是上帝的礼物,那么与它慷慨相处是什么样子?” 和信仰一样 善良的心是肯和莎莉成长的

肯记得父亲给了他钱放进祭品盘中,莎莉记得看着她的父母不仅把钱送给他们的教堂,还送给需要帮助的人和组织. Sally的父亲特别喜欢匿名赠送。 肯和莎莉已经长大了, 他们已经了解到慷慨不只是给予一定的百分比或检查一个盒子。

需要不断问, 对肯来说,慷慨意味着什么的问题已经变成了他所谓的“提高国王地位”的问题。 当他考虑施舍的时候,他问道:"这难道是为了真主的荣耀而推动王国吗? 这个问题决定了夫妻双方对哪些个人和组织的看法

title: Scripture Translation Invigorates Majority World Believers
source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
summary: Today on the Faithly Podcast, Alicia Lee welcomes Melissa Paredes, Senior Director of Content Marketing at Wycliffe Bible Translators USA, for a meaningful conversation about Bible translation, motherhood, and the life-changing power of Scripture.   The post  Scripture Translation Invigorates Majority World Believers  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
summary_zh: 今天，在Faithly播客上， Alicia Lee欢迎Wycliffe Bible Translators USA内容营销高级总监Melissa Paredes就圣经翻译、母性以及圣经改变生活的力量进行有意义的对话。后圣经翻译激励大多数世界信徒首先出现在威克里夫。
title_zh: 圣经翻译激励世界大多数信徒
content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now
